sections.h2: How should a Marietta owner approach a sale?
sections.html:
Owners here usually pick between an agent listing, a self-managed sale and a straight cash purchase. Repair needs and your calendar decide which of the three fits.

  • Agent listing: reaches buyers who rely on mortgages, which means showings, inspection requests and a closing date set by their lender.
  • For sale by owner: the agent's share stays with you, and so do pricing, marketing and negotiation.
  • Cash buyer: a quicker close without a repair list, at a price that reflects current condition.

With typical home values at $448,500, a small gap in percentage between two offers is a large gap in cash. Get each offer's terms in writing before comparing.

Marietta's population is about 63,574 in the mid-2025 estimate, a 4.1% rise over the 61,060 used as the 2020 starting point. Owners live in 47.2% of homes, so renters fill the rest. Monthly owner costs run $2,170 with a mortgage and $618 without, and median gross rent is $1,586. The city has 24,707 households averaging 2.40 people.

Owners of older houses near the Square should ask the city which exterior changes need approval in the historic district before promising a buyer any work. Code Enforcement covers that district along with zoning and signs.

The City of Marietta enforces the 2024 editions of the International Building Code and International Residential Code, with 2026 Georgia amendments, for projects permitted after January 1, 2026. Plumbing, mechanical and fuel gas codes follow the 2024 editions as well, and the electrical code is the 2023 National Electrical Code with 2026 Georgia amendments.

All building permits are submitted online. Pulling a permit before repairs matters at sale time, because a buyer's inspector or title review may turn up unpermitted work. The Building Inspection Division answers questions at 770-794-5659.

Code Enforcement checks building code, zoning, signs, the historic district and the standard housing code. It sits at 205 Lawrence Street, phone 770-794-5439, and it can act only on properties inside the city limits. A Marietta mailing address does not guarantee the house is inside the city, so use the city's Property Search Tool to confirm which rules apply.

sections.h2: Cobb County property tax and Marietta's city bill
sections.html:
Cobb's Tax Commissioner bills for the county government and the school district. The seven cities inside Cobb, Marietta among them, run their own billing, so ask the City of Marietta about its separate portion.

Cobb tax year milestones
StepRule
Assessment dateEach January 1 sets who owes for the year
Personal property returnsDue at the Tax Assessor's office by April 1
Bills mailedBy August 15
Payment dueOn or before October 15
Late payment5% penalty plus monthly interest

The county does not split the bill between seller and buyer. Who owes what is set by the closing paperwork, and the purchaser generally takes on the liability. The tax is figured for the full year and follows the property.

The Tax Commissioner accepts partial payments and will honor a U.S. Post Office postmark dated by midnight of the deadline. Metered or kiosk postage does not count. An owner appealing a value must still pay at least the appeal amount by the due date. Pay at 736 Whitlock Avenue, Suite 100, Marietta, or by mail to PO Box 100127, Marietta, GA 30061. The office phone is 770-528-8600. Bills for 2026 also carry the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant, which is separate from homestead exemptions.

Drop boxes sit outside the Whitlock Avenue office, and the East Cobb and South Cobb Government Service Centers take payments too.

Buyers can try the Tax Commissioner's estimator for new home purchasers: enter a fair market value, choose the city or unincorporated tax district and select exemptions. The tool applies the 40% assessed value rule from O.C.G.A. 48-5-7 and covers county taxes only, so a buyer still has to ask the city for its own figure. Sellers can use it to show a buyer what the county side of the bill is likely to look like.

After the last day for payment, Cobb notifies the taxpayer in writing. Unless the taxes are paid within thirty days, an execution called a fi. fa. may be issued under O.C.G.A. 48-3-3. Taxes legally attach to the property, so settle any balance early.

Tax sales run on the first Tuesday of each month in which a sale is planned, held on the Superior Courthouse steps at Flournoy Park in Marietta between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Cobb publishes a Tax Sale Booklet on the process. If you are behind, call 770-528-8600 about payment arrangements before the sale date. Partial payments are accepted, though penalty and interest keep accruing on the balance.

The Cobb clerk records the deed only after the state transfer tax is paid and a PT-61 is filed. Georgia's rate is $1 on the first $1,000 or any fraction of it, and 10 cents on each further $100 or fraction of $100.

Legal liability sits with the seller unless the contract moves it. After the sale, the new owner will need the recorded deed to reapply for a homestead exemption. Your own exemption ends at the sale, and Cobb asks owners who sold or moved to tell the Tax Commissioner, since failing to report can bring a penalty.

sections.h2: From signed contract to closing day
sections.html:
Once a contract is signed, the work shifts to paperwork. Your closing attorney or title company pulls the Cobb bill and asks the city for its portion. They also confirm that no execution has been issued on the parcel. Because the county tax is figured for the full year and follows the property, the settlement statement should show clearly who covers which stretch of the year.

If you are selling to a cash buyer, the same steps apply, only faster, because no lender is waiting on an appraisal. If you appeal a value while a sale is pending, remember that you must still pay at least the appeal amount by the due date.

Gather the deed, your mortgage payoff figure, the latest Cobb and city tax bills and permit records for any repair. Confirm the house is inside city limits so you know whose rules and bills apply. A cash buyer will look at the same papers, though the buyer's price will reflect the house as it stands. A listing buyer's lender will want a clean title and settled tax bills, so clear any balance before an offer comes in.

faqs.q: Who covers Cobb property tax when a Marietta house closes?
faqs.a: The contract and settlement statement decide. The Tax Commissioner does not prorate between the parties, and liability generally passes to the purchaser.

faqs.q: What is the payment deadline on a Cobb tax bill?
faqs.a: October 15, with bills mailed by August 15. After that a 5% penalty applies and interest builds monthly. Marietta's own city bill is separate, so ask the city for that date.

faqs.q: Can I get a Marietta building permit online?
faqs.a: Yes. The city takes all permits online, and its Building Inspection Division at 770-794-5659 can answer questions. Code Enforcement at 770-794-5439 handles complaints inside city limits only.

faqs.q: Is every Marietta mailing address inside city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. A Marietta mailing address does not place a property inside the limits. The city's Property Search Tool shows which government's rules apply.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: It ends. Cobb asks owners who no longer qualify, including those who sold or moved, to tell the Tax Commissioner. The buyer applies separately.
